skill.name: workday-careers-site-job-listings-extractor
skill.description: Extract public Workday job listings through a hosted Apify Actor, with documented keyword, location, date, and remote-work filters.
skill.summary: Configure a hosted Workday extraction run and retrieve job listings as JSON through a Node.js runner or documented API calls.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

security_audit.summary: All 64 static findings are false positives in context: documented API authentication, expected input reads, public URLs, and formatting mistaken for execution. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, unauthorized exfiltration, or system reconnaissance in the supplied files. The hosted Actor implementation is not included, so its runtime behavior was not verified.

content.value_statement: Collecting public Workday vacancies manually makes recurring job research time-consuming. This skill provides input guidance and API examples for a hosted Apify extractor.
actual_capabilities: Provides a Node.js runner that submits JSON input to Apify and prints the returned dataset as formatted JSON.
Documents careers-site URL, tenant, and direct job URL modes for the hosted extractor.
Defines keyword, location, job family, posting-date, and remote-only filter inputs.
Documents optional full-detail fetching and job-family enrichment through the hosted Actor.
Lists title, tenant, location, postedOn, timeType, and workplaceType as dataset fields.
Provides curl examples for synchronous extraction, asynchronous run creation, status checks, and dataset retrieval.
limitations: Extraction depends on a hosted Apify Actor whose implementation is not included in the supplied files.
The Node.js runner requires Node 18+, an APIFY_TOKEN, network access, and an Apify account that covers usage charges.
The documented synchronous endpoint waits up to 300 seconds; the runner does not implement asynchronous polling or retries.
Only public postings are in scope; field availability depends on employer data, and the runner outputs JSON rather than CSV.

use_cases.title: Find Relevant Public Vacancies
use_cases.description: Request a limited set of jobs from an employer careers site using keyword, location, and posting-date filters.

use_cases.title: Compare Employer Hiring Activity
use_cases.description: Collect public listings with consistent filters for later comparison of locations, categories, and work arrangements.

use_cases.title: Prepare Recruitment Data Imports
use_cases.description: Retrieve a bounded JSON dataset of public vacancies for a separate reporting or recruitment workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Collect a Small Sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract up to 25 public jobs from [Workday careers URL]. Use careerSite mode and disable full details and job-family enrichment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect a small listing sample.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Recent Vacancies
prompt_templates.prompt: Find jobs matching [keyword] in [location] at [Workday careers URL], posted within 7 days. Limit results to 25 and summarize returned fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: narrow a public job search.

prompt_templates.title: Request Remote Job Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Use tenant [tenant] and site [site]. Set remoteOnly to true and maxItems to 25. Retrieve details and identify missing employer fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine tenant targeting and detail-dependent filtering.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Larger Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an asynchronous run for [Workday careers URLs] with maxItems 500. Explain shared-cap ordering and confirm expected charges before submission.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan a larger, cost-aware API workflow.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: summarize a returned engineering listing.
output: This example is illustrative, not a verified live vacancy.

output_examples.input: Explain the configured limits for two careers URLs with maxItems set to 25.
output: The limit applies across both URLs, not separately to each site.
Jobs are returned in URL order.
The first site can consume the entire 25-job allowance.

best_practices: Start with maxItems set to 25, inspect returned fields, and check current Actor pricing before increasing the limit.
Keep APIFY_TOKEN in the environment and submit only intended public careers inputs, never cookies, sessions, or private account data.
Check site terms and applicable law, and confirm asynchronous completion before retrieving results from a large run.
anti_patterns: Using the extractor for login-protected listings or submitting private account data.
Expecting local extraction, guaranteed field completeness, or native CSV output from the Node.js runner.
Increasing collection limits without checking costs, site permissions, and the shared cap across URLs.

faq.question: Does this skill scrape Workday locally?
faq.answer: No. The local runner sends input to a hosted Apify Actor and prints its returned dataset.

faq.question: What do I need to run it?
faq.answer: The Node.js runner requires Node 18+, APIFY_TOKEN, and network access. Apify bills Actor usage to your account.

faq.question: Can I target a tenant instead of a URL?
faq.answer: Yes. The input schema documents tenant mode with a tenant name, optional site identifier, and automatic or specified region.

faq.question: How are remote jobs selected?
faq.answer: The documented remoteOnly option keeps employer-labeled remote jobs, excludes hybrid and onsite postings, and enables full detail fetching.

faq.question: Does the runner export CSV?
faq.answer: No. The supplied runner prints JSON. CSV conversion requires a separate step.

faq.question: How should I handle larger runs?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous API flow and confirm completion before retrieving the dataset. The local runner only uses the synchronous endpoint.
